model_annotation: Figure 3(a) presents a line plot comparing the training loss versus training steps for five different model configurations: Vanilla (black line with circle markers), StrmLM (n=64, blue line with square markers), SepLLM (n=64, red line with diamond markers), SepLLM (n=64, H/T, green line with triangle markers), and SepLLM (n=128, purple line with star markers). The x-axis, labeled “Training steps,” spans from 0 to 140,000 in linear scale, with major tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis, labeled “Loss,” ranges from approximately 2.5 to 4.5, also on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.5. All lines exhibit a downward trend, indicating decreasing loss over training steps. The Vanilla model starts at a loss of approximately 4.4 and declines to about 2.8 by 140,000 steps. StrmLM (n=64) begins near 4.2 and ends around 2.9. SepLLM (n=64) starts at ~4.1 and ends at ~2.75. SepLLM (n=64, H/T) begins at ~4.0 and drops to ~2.7. SepLLM (n=128) starts at ~3.9 and reaches ~2.65 by the final step, showing the lowest final loss among all methods. The lines are closely spaced at the beginning but diverge slightly as training progresses, with SepLLM (n=128) consistently maintaining the lowest loss after approximately 20,000 steps.
